subject: Post-call: tailored eval plan & scoring rubric for OptimaHealth integration
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@optimahealth.com>, Jared Kim <jared.kim@optimahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: tailored eval plan & scoring rubric for OptimaHealth integration

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about OptimaHealth's triage and clinical decision support flows. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can get an Eval run scheduled on Redwood and validate model fit for your live workload: 

Recap (0-5 min):
- Goal: automated triage suggestions and short-form clinical summarization for PCP handoff. Primary concerns: accuracy (avoid hallucination), response latency (<400ms p95), and safety (PII handling + medical correctness).
- Data: you can provide de-identified historical triage transcripts + clinician notes (~7k rows available initially).

Recommended model candidates (starting list for benchmarks):
- redwood-13b-chat-gptq (low-latency baseline)
- meta-llama-2-70b-chat (high-capacity baseline)
- open-instruct-7b (cost-efficient baseline)

What I'm attaching: seed prompt set and a suggested data schema (optima_eval_seed_prompts.csv, optima_data_schema.json). These are sample rows + column descriptions to speed onboarding.

Proposed Eval plan + timing:
1) You deliver a 1k-row development sample (JSONL or CSV) with the schema in optima_data_schema.json by EOD Thu 11/6.
2) Redwood runs an initial automated benchmark against the three model candidates (3–4 business days).
3) We run a focused human-eval slice (100 cases) for safety and hallucination review and produce a scoring report and suggested prompt/quantization profile.

Scoring & pass/fail signal (high level) — we should align before you upload:
- Closed Q / classification: Exact Match (EM) and F1 where appropriate.
- Free-text summarization: ROUGE-L and human avg rating (scale 1-5) for clinical fidelity.
- Hallucination metric: human-check rate (percent of cases flagged for factual errors).
- Latency: p95 token latency target <400ms for redwood-13b-chat; note larger models will have higher latency.

Next steps I need from you:
- Confirm the 1k sample delivery date (EOD Thu 11/6).
- Indicate any regulatory constraints for hosting (must be AWS us-east-1, KMS key required, or on-prem?).
- Point person for data upload + procurement contact for contract/PO.

I'll loop in Solutions (Rishi) and Customer Success (Marissa) who will follow with the exact upload instructions and scoring rubric. If that timeline works, I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Fri 11/7 to align expectations and label assignment for the human-eval slice.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0128

Subject: Re: Post-call: tailored eval plan & scoring rubric for OptimaHealth integration

Thanks, Tessa — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Dataset: we can deliver a 1k de-identified sample by EOD Thu 11/6 (confirmed). The full historical set is ~7k rows but we'll start with 1k.
- PII & compliance: all PHI will be redacted; Optima needs to confirm whether Redwood will store the dataset for longer than 30 days during the eval. We prefer minimal retention.
- Procurement: procurement@optimahealth.com will need an SOW and rough estimate prior to signing. Can you attach the SOW in your next email?

Also: what does the human-eval process look like — will Optima provide clinicians for labeling or will Redwood manage the human raters? If Redwood manages, can you share reviewer qualifications?

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Martinez
Director of Product, OptimaHealth
sofia.martinez@optimahealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@optimahealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: tailored eval plan & scoring rubric for OptimaHealth integration

Hi Sofia — quick answers and the concrete upload/config steps so your engineering team can move quickly.

1) Data format (required for Redwood Eval-run):
- Preferred: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL). Each record should be one JSON object with fields: 
  - id: string (unique)
  - input: string (raw triage transcript OR clinician prompt)
  - reference: string (ground-truth triage label or clinician summary)
  - metadata: string or map (optional JSON string with age_band, dept, deidentified_patient_id)

Sample row (single-line JSON):
{"id":"row-0001","input":"Patient reports chest pain for 2 hours...","reference":"Urgent: refer to ED; possible MI; recommended urgent EKG","metadata":"{\"age_band\":\"45-54\",\"dept\":\"teletriage\"}"}

If you can't produce JSONL, CSV with columns id,input,reference,metadata is acceptable. We included a sample CSV in the attachment.

2) Upload: use the secure S3 bucket we provisioned for your deal. Temporary upload link (placeholders in related_links) — send the signed SOW and our engineering team will open a one-time presigned PUT. We will not retain data longer than 30 days by default; retention policies are configurable per deal.

3) Scoring rubric (automated + human):
- Automated metrics we run by default: Exact Match (EM), token F1, BLEU, ROUGE-L. These run against the 'reference' field.
- Human evaluation: 5-point Likert scale across three axes: clinical fidelity, hallucination risk, and safety/PII leakage. Each case flagged for hallucination gets a short note describing the error type.
- Pass thresholds (initial recommendations):
  - Closed-item EM > 0.75 for production-readiness on structured triage output.
  - Summarization: ROUGE-L > 0.60 and human avg >= 4.0 across fidelity.
  - Hallucination: human-flag rate < 5% on the 100-case sample.

4) Eval job config we suggest (we'll provision defaults, you can override via API):
- models: [redwood-13b-chat-gptq, meta-llama-2-70b-chat, open-instruct-7b]
- batch_size: 16
- concurrency: 4
- sample_slice_for_human_eval: 100 (stratified by age_band + department)
- store_kv_cache: false for scoring runs

5) Human raters: Redwood can staff clinicians with prior triage experience for the human-eval slice (we have an existing panel). If Optima prefers to use internal clinicians, we can provide the labeling UI and a labeling guide; we'll combine internal labels with our panel for inter-rater reliability checks.

I'll attach a short JSON config template and the expected CSV/JSONL schema in the attachments. Once you upload the sample, ping me and we'll kick off the automated run and schedule the human-eval window.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
